answer.rationale: The binding constraints are timing (14 days, no auto-renew) and zero delivery buffer at 94% of committed volume. Any action that touches physical supply continuity — switching primary vendor (memory_c2) or standing up a second source (memory_c3) — requires onboarding and qualification time we do not have inside 14 days, and would put delivery risk up against an explicit objective to hold it flat. Deferring (memory_c5) worked for a non-critical service on month-to-month terms; this contract does not auto-renew, so deferral here means lapse, not extension. That leaves the incumbent, and a bare renewal (memory_c1) buys stability but no path to an 18% cut. Negotiating at renewal (memory_c4) is the only direction that attacks cost without moving atoms, and memory_c6 suggests a multi-year commitment is a lever available inside that negotiation. I want the source record for memory_c4 to see what the recovered margin actually was — 'real margin' may be a few points on payment terms, well short of 18%, in which case negotiation alone does not clear the mandate and I need to know that before committing rather than after. I want memory_c2 because it is the loudest cost signal in memory and the one most likely to be misread: it says 'last year,' it says nothing about the constrained component or about lead time to qualify, and if its onboarding was quick because it was a low-volume or non-critical line, it does not transfer to primary supply under a no-buffer line. Verifying it is how I avoid letting an attractive cost number override the delivery constraint. Downstream risk flagged: these memories are consolidated summaries that record outcomes without the conditions that produced them, and the aggregate of them mildly favors the incumbent simply because four of six entries involve the incumbent — that is a sampling artifact of what got written down, not evidence about the market. If negotiation lands materially short of 18%, the correct next-cycle move is a qualified second source or dual-track vendor evaluation started now on a small guarded basis, not an emergency switch; I am recording that so the gap is not treated as closed.
